status: Source review only; no new runtime or allocation measurements
findings: PiLaurentPolynomial::clone_with_work first pays a node visit, then allocates a vector sized to its term count. The normal form has an eight-term local limit. Each coefficient clone preflights its rational, radical and atom coefficient storage before cloning that coefficient.

The vector allocation is therefore statically bounded in retained normal forms. Earlier coefficient clones can be completed before a later coefficient debit fails, but their own coefficient reads were charged first. This ordering alone does not establish a width-dependent public resource failure or violate the stated cooperative-unit contract.

The clone helper is used for shared-node memo hits, retaining memo results, and existing-term arithmetic. A proposed preflight-all-terms rewrite would add traversal or debit work and must preserve ordinary-path cost, existing successful proofs and all local limits.

The existing Laurent allowance sweep preserves root facts, unlimited retry and zero-work proof reuse, and includes a deliberately shared binomial. It does not measure allocation boundaries for the standalone polynomial clone.
next_measurement: If pursued, compare zero, just-insufficient and sufficient clone allowances for one through eight terms, early/late wide rational/radical/atom coefficients, and a separately established public memo-hit path. Classify a bounded paid allocation as already bounded unless evidence establishes a requirement failure; do not introduce a zero-allocation requirement merely to justify a repair.
